chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Upon the one performing Tamattu' with Umrah to Hajj are three circumambulations of the House, and he prays two cycles for each circumambulation, and two Sa'ees between As-Safa and Al-Marwa.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: One performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What are the required rituals for Hajj al-Tamattu' regarding Tawaf and Sa'ee?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the reliable chain of Ibn Abi Umayr, clarifies the ritual structure of Hajj al-Tamattu' by distinguishing the Umrah rites from the Hajj rites. It establishes that the pilgrim must perform three complete cycles of Tawaf and Sa’ee—two for Umrah and one for Hajj—each accompanied by the two-rak'ah prayer, a practice that underscores the distinct legal status of each pilgrimage phase in Shia jurisprudence. This detailed breakdown ensures the validity of the 'enjoyment' type of Hajj by preventing the conflation of the two separate obligations.
